page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7571 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and an 8 MB L3 cache slice. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, and SHA extensions, while omitting AVX-512. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest computational performance consistent with its burstable allocation model. Stress-ng scores reached 566.4 for single-core and 1181.97 for multi-core tests, placing compute throughput in the lower percentiles. Geekbench results reflect similar trends with a single-core score of 692.0 and multi-core score of 1674.0. PassMark CPU execution delivered an overall score of 3622.97, though encryption tasks reached an average tier at 3207.35 points due to dedicated cryptographic acceleration. Memory throughput tests recorded 23.87 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 11.7 GB/sec for writes. Database and key-value metrics include 2.53 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and a PassMark database score of 938.34.

The primary tradeoff of the t3a.xlarge is its reliance on burstable CPU credits and an older generation AMD processor, resulting in lower raw compute and memory bandwidth compared to dedicated compute instances. However, it delivers high cost efficiency for environments with intermittent computational needs. The instance fits small to medium web servers, development environments, background job processors, staging clusters, and low-traffic enterprise internal services that do not require continuous sustained compute.

The instance has no local instance storage and relies on a 1 Gbps baseline network connection without GPU acceleration.
